nodes.description: Public pure library function that removes the element at idx from a uint256 array by copying it and shifting the remaining elements, returning the new array.
Input uint256 array from which one element is removed.
Index of the element to be removed; used by the shifting loop and array reads.
Memory array produced by copy(array, array.length-1) and then overwritten with shifted elements.
Public pure library function allocating a new uint256 memory array and copying up to len elements from the source array.
Source uint256 array copied element by element.
Requested copy length, clamped to array.length inside the function.
Newly allocated memory array holding the copied values.
Public pure library function computing a positional hash of a uint256 array using base 100 powers.
Input uint256 array whose elements are multiplied by increasing powers of baseStep.
Running power of baseStep (100), multiplied every iteration and able to grow without bound.
Accumulated hash value, sum of array[i]*pow, unchecked against uint256 limits.
Unchecked multiplication array[i]*pow and accumulation into ans can silently overflow/wrap uint256 because Solidity 0.4.24 arithmetic is unchecked.
Public pure library function returning true when the target address appears in the address array.
Address array iterated over by the membership check.
Target address compared against every element of adrs.
Public view library pseudo-random generator mixing blockhash, coinbase, difficulty, gaslimit, now/timestamp, tx.origin and the caller-provided mixed value, returning hashVal % max.
Upper bound used as the divisor of hashVal % max; a zero value would revert.
Caller supplied entropy added into hashVal (19*mixed).
Accumulator of block/environment entropy that is finally reduced modulo max; grows as a uint256 sum.
block.number - 1, used as the input of blockhash.
Block timestamp (also referenced as now) is added into hashVal, making the random result miner-influenceable and timestamp dependent.
Transaction origin address is added into hashVal, making the random result dependent on the external caller identity.
hashVal % max produces a value derivable from public on-chain data, so the pseudo-random output is predictable and manipulable by miners/callers.
Public pure library function returning the identity array [0,1,...,len-1].
Length of the generated index array.
Memory array filled with consecutive indices using a uint128 loop counter.
Public view library function generating 'digits' random indices by repeatedly calling random on a shrinking index array via removeByIdx.
Number of random indices to generate and size of the output array.
Length of the index template passed to getIdxArray.
Offset added to the loop counter when seeding the random call.
Output array holding the generated random indices.
Working copy of the index array, shrunk with removeByIdx after each draw.

edges.reason: Parameter array is read by removeByIdx to build the shifted result.
Parameter idx drives the shifting while-loop and array indexing in removeByIdx.
removeByIdx writes the shifted values into its local memory array ans.
removeByIdx passes the input array into ArrayUtils.copy.
The array returned by copy becomes the ans array that removeByIdx mutates.
copy reads elements from its source array parameter.
Parameter len sets the copy bound after being clamped to array.length.
copy fills its local memory array ans with the copied elements.
getHash iterates over the input array and reads every element.
pow = pow * baseStep is unchecked and can overflow uint256.
ans = ans + array[i]*pow is unchecked and can overflow uint256.
The unsafe arithmetic is executed inside getHash's loop body.
contains scans the provided address array.
The target address is compared against each element in contains.
block.timestamp entropy is mixed into hashVal, making random timestamp dependent.
tx.origin entropy is mixed into hashVal, making random dependent on the originating account.
Parameter max is the divisor of the final hashVal % max computation.
hashVal is reduced modulo max, yielding a deterministic and predictable pseudo-random value.
lastBlockNumber feeds blockhash, whose value is accumulated into hashVal.
The caller-provided mixed value is added into hashVal.
The modulo operation produces random's return value, completing its control flow.
genRandomArray calls CommUtils.random to draw each index.
templateLen is forwarded to getIdxArray as its length argument.
Parameter len determines the size of the identity index array.
getIdxArray fills its local array ans with consecutive indices.
The array returned by getIdxArray is assigned to genRandomArray's local variable idxs.
idxs.removeByIdx(idx) invokes ArrayUtils.removeByIdx on the working index array.
digits bounds the generation loop and the output array size.
base is added to the loop counter when seeding each random call.
genRandomArray writes each drawn index into its local output array ans.

Index parameter used solely for the shift loop inside removeByIdx.
Temporary local of removeByIdx holding the returned array.
Source parameter read only inside copy.
Length parameter only bounded and used inside copy.
Temporary local returned by copy.
Input array is only iterated inside getHash.
Running power participates directly in the unchecked multiplication overflow.
Accumulator participates directly in the unchecked addition overflow.
Address array scanned only inside contains.
Search target used only for comparison inside contains.
max is the divisor of the final modulo whose result is predictable.
Caller entropy parameter added into hashVal inside random.
hashVal is the value reduced modulo max to produce the random output.
Temporary used only as blockhash input inside random.
Length parameter sizing the identity array built by getIdxArray.
Local array returned by getIdxArray.
Loop bound and output size parameter of genRandomArray.
Template length parameter only forwarded to getIdxArray.
Seed offset parameter used only inside the generation loop.
Local output array of genRandomArray.
Working index array used only inside genRandomArray's loop.
